title: Zero-shot doubled-consonant respelling — phonetic retrieves it, exact cannot
why_real: The user has only ever entered the respelled name as a standing dictionary entry, never spoken a sentence the system saw as a correction, so the very first utterance that uses the plain-spelling variant has to be caught by sound rather than by an exact string it has already seen.

expected.reason: Phonetic retrieval closes the zero-shot doubled-consonant gap (ayushman/ayushmann share a metaphone key) and applies; exact has never seen the surface 'ayushman' as a stored form, so it abstains no_memory.
